preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the tree is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= c_i <= 10**9 for c_i in c) and len(c) == n
preconditions.description: Each vertex has a non-negative price (0 ≤ c_i ≤ 10^9), and there are exactly n prices.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n for a, b in edges)
preconditions.description: The tree has exactly n-1 edges, and each edge connects two vertices in the range [1, n].
The edges form a valid tree with root at vertex 1 (no cycles, connected, and root is vertex 1).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [str(s), str(k)] and len(lines) == 2 and lines[1].strip().split() == sorted(optimal_vertices)
postconditions.description: The first line of stdout contains two integers: the minimum total cost s and the number of vertices k in at least one optimal set. The second line contains k distinct vertex indices in increasing order that belong to at least one optimal set.

postconditions.expression: s == min_cost and all(vertex in optimal_sets for vertex in optimal_vertices)
postconditions.description: The minimum cost s is the smallest total price of a non-empty set of vertices such that Arkady can guarantee all leaf values are zeroed regardless of Vasily's input. The set of optimal vertices are those appearing in at least one such optimal set.

postconditions.expression: len(optimal_vertices) == k and all(1 <= v <= n for v in optimal_vertices)
postconditions.description: The number of optimal vertices k matches the count of distinct vertices in optimal_vertices, and all vertices are within the valid range [1, n].
